title: Lead with the result
why: Showing the outcome first makes people stay to find out how you got there.
formula: [The result] in [the time or effort it took]. Here's what changed.
check: Mute the first second. Can a stranger see the result before you explain anything?

hooks.say: This edit took me eleven minutes. Last month the same thing ate my whole Sunday.
hooks.frame: Tight on your face, with the finished video playing on the laptop behind you.
hooks.next: Flash the old timeline for one second, then name the single change that made the difference.

hooks.say: I paid off my credit card in seven months on a normal salary, and there was no side hustle.
hooks.frame: Your face, then the zero balance full screen with you in a corner circle.
hooks.next: Say the one rule you followed, in one sentence, before any backstory.

hooks.say: This is my latte art after two weeks. All I changed was how I hold the jug.
hooks.frame: Close on the finished pour with the pattern fully formed.
hooks.next: Cut to your hand on the jug and show the old grip next to the new one.

hooks.say: Same desk, same camera. This video got forty times my usual views, and I only changed the first two seconds.
hooks.frame: Split screen: the old video's view count on top, the new one below.
hooks.next: Play the two openings back to back so viewers can spot the difference themselves.

hooks.say: I built this table with three tools and no workshop. The cheapest one mattered most.
hooks.frame: Hands sanding the finished tabletop in one smooth pass.
hooks.next: Lay the three tools out and point at the cheap one first.

hooks.say: My screen time went from nine hours to two, and I didn't delete a single app.
hooks.frame: Your phone's screen-time page, held up to the camera.
hooks.next: Show the one setting you changed, on the phone screen, before explaining why it worked.

hooks.say: This is what my notes look like now. I can find anything in under ten seconds.
hooks.frame: Over the shoulder as you flip straight to a tabbed page.
hooks.next: Time yourself finding an old note on camera, then explain the tab system.

hooks.say: We got our first hundred customers without spending anything on ads. This is the post that did it.
hooks.frame: The post full screen, your face in a lower corner.
hooks.next: Point at the one line in the post that got people to message you.

hooks.say: That's the footage straight off my phone. This is after a ten-second fix in the camera settings.
hooks.frame: Before and after of the same shot, stacked.
hooks.next: Open the camera settings and show the exact toggle.

hooks.say: This shirt took me one evening, and I'd never sewn anything before last month.
hooks.frame: The machine stitching the last seam, fabric filling the frame.
hooks.next: Hold up the finished shirt, then admit the part that took three tries.

title: Call out the mistake
why: People stop scrolling for something they might be getting wrong right now.
formula: If you [common habit], [what it's costing you].
check: Does the first line name a habit the viewer recognizes in under two seconds?

hooks.say: If your captions sit at the bottom of the screen, Instagram's buttons are covering half of them.
hooks.frame: A phone showing a Reel with the app's buttons over the captions.
hooks.next: Move the captions up on the same clip and show the difference.

hooks.say: You're filming at eye level and wondering why it looks flat. Raise the camera two inches.
hooks.frame: You reaching up and adjusting the camera mid-sentence.
hooks.next: Cut between the low and raised angle twice so the change is obvious.

hooks.say: Stop saving your best tip for the end. Most people are gone by then.
hooks.text: They left before your best tip
hooks.frame: Your face, then a retention graph sloping down with you in a corner circle.
hooks.next: Show where the graph drops and say where you should have put the tip.

hooks.say: If you chop garlic and throw it straight in the pan, you're losing most of the flavor. Give it ten minutes.
hooks.frame: The knife finishing the last chop on the board.
hooks.next: Show the timer on the counter and what you do while it rests.

hooks.say: You're sanding with the grain and still getting scratches because you skipped a grit.
hooks.frame: The sander mid-pass, close on the wood.
hooks.next: Lay the sandpaper out in order and run your hand over each finish.

hooks.say: If you answer every client message within a minute, you've trained them to expect it.
hooks.text: You trained them to do this
hooks.frame: A phone lighting up with three messages in a row.
hooks.next: Show the reply you send now, and the hours you set.

hooks.say: Your first sentence is 'Hey guys, welcome back.' That's exactly where people swipe.
hooks.frame: Your face, then the words crossed out across the frame.
hooks.next: Re-record the opening without it and play the new version.

hooks.say: If your latte art spreads into a blob, your milk is too hot, not too thin.
hooks.frame: A blobby pour spreading across the cup.
hooks.next: Put a thermometer in the jug and pour again at the right temperature.

hooks.say: You're shooting video on auto exposure, and that's why your face keeps flickering.
hooks.frame: A thumb turning the camera dial, close.
hooks.next: Show the exact setting and a clip before and after you locked it.

hooks.say: If you write your hook after you film, you're filming the wrong video.
hooks.frame: You crossing out a page in your notebook.
hooks.next: Show the hook written at the top of a fresh page and the shots planned under it.

title: Say the unpopular thing
why: A respectful disagreement with common advice makes people want to hear your reason.
check: Can you back the claim up within the next ten seconds?

hooks.say: Stop putting music under your talking-head videos. Your voice is the soundtrack.
hooks.frame: Your face, with a music track that cuts to silence.
hooks.next: Play the same clip with and without music and let viewers hear it.

hooks.say: Posting every day made my channel worse. This is what I do instead.
hooks.frame: Your face, then a full calendar with the days crossed out.
hooks.next: Show your new schedule on screen in one line.

hooks.say: You don't need a better camera. You need a window and a cheap reflector.
hooks.frame: You turning toward a window as the light on your face changes.
hooks.next: Hold a white card up to your face and show the shadow soften.

hooks.say: Meal prep Sunday is the reason you're bored of your food by Wednesday.
hooks.frame: A stack of identical containers, then a fresh pan.
hooks.next: Show what you cook ahead instead: parts, not meals.

hooks.say: I stopped using to-do apps and went back to paper. I get more done.
hooks.frame: A hand writing a three-line list in a notebook.
hooks.next: Show yesterday's list with every line crossed off.

hooks.say: Trending audio is why your Reel sounds like everyone else's.
hooks.frame: A phone scrolling past three Reels with the same sound.
hooks.next: Play your Reel with your own voice up front instead.

hooks.say: The best editing advice I ever got was to cut less, not more.
hooks.frame: Your face; a crowded timeline behind you thinning out.
hooks.next: Show one scene cut fast, then cut slower, and say which one held you.

hooks.say: Morning routines are overrated. What you do at ten at night matters more.
hooks.frame: The clock on your phone showing 10:00 PM.
hooks.next: Walk through the three things you do before bed, quickly.

hooks.say: Everyone tells you to charge more. I raised my prices and lost my best clients.
hooks.frame: Your face, then an invoice with the old rate crossed out.
hooks.next: Say what you'd change if you raised them again tomorrow.

hooks.say: Ten thousand steps is a nice round number. It's not a magic one.
hooks.frame: Feet hitting the pavement in a steady rhythm.
hooks.next: Say where the number came from, then what you aim for instead.

title: Start mid-story
why: Dropping the viewer into the middle of something makes them need the next line.
formula: [A time marker], [the moment things went wrong or changed].
check: Does the first sentence start after the boring part of the story?

hooks.say: Three days before launch, our only editor quit.
hooks.frame: Your face, close, no smile, phone in hand.
hooks.next: Say what was left to finish, as a short list on screen.

hooks.say: The client watched the first draft, said nothing for ten seconds, and then asked who made it.
hooks.frame: Over the shoulder on a laptop playing the draft.
hooks.next: Reveal whether that was good or bad before explaining anything.

hooks.say: I was halfway up the stairs with the camera when I realized there was no card in it.
hooks.frame: Shoes climbing the steps, fast.
hooks.next: Cut to what you filmed instead, on your phone.

hooks.say: My landlord texted me a photo of my own front door. That's when I knew.
hooks.frame: A phone in hand with the message open.
hooks.next: Explain what the photo showed in one line, then rewind to how it started.

hooks.say: The first table I ever sold came back two weeks later with a crack down the middle.
hooks.frame: Hands running over a freshly sanded tabletop.
hooks.next: Show the crack, then the mistake that caused it.

hooks.say: I opened my analytics, saw one video at two million views, and didn't even recognize it.
hooks.frame: A phone showing a view count climbing.
hooks.next: Play the first two seconds of that video.

hooks.say: On my first day at the café, I ruined forty lattes before lunch.
hooks.frame: Milk pouring into a cup, a little too fast.
hooks.next: Show the one thing the head barista told you that afternoon.

hooks.say: I was editing at two in the morning when the timeline froze and took six hours of work with it.
hooks.frame: A laptop screen, cursor spinning.
hooks.next: Show the setting that would have saved it.

hooks.say: My mum called after watching my video and asked one question I couldn't answer.
hooks.frame: You with the phone to your ear, looking off camera.
hooks.next: Say the question on screen, then start answering it.

hooks.say: We were five minutes into the interview when the guest leaned in and said, 'Can I be honest?'
hooks.frame: The guest leaning into the microphone.
hooks.next: Play their next sentence uncut.

title: Promise a number
why: A number tells people exactly how much time they're signing up for.
check: Can you deliver every item in the time the viewer expects?

hooks.say: Three cuts that save a boring talking-head take. The last one takes two seconds.
hooks.frame: Your face with a 1/3 counter in the corner.
hooks.next: Go straight into cut number one with no intro.

hooks.say: Four settings I change on every new phone before I film anything.
hooks.frame: A thumb scrolling through the camera settings.
hooks.next: Show setting one on screen, zoomed in, within the first three seconds.

hooks.say: Five things in my kitchen I'd buy again tomorrow, and one I regret.
hooks.frame: A knife finishing a chop on the board.
hooks.next: Start with the one you'd buy first, and save the regret for last.

hooks.say: Two sentences I use to turn down work without burning the bridge.
hooks.frame: Your face, then the message full screen with you in a corner.
hooks.next: Read sentence one aloud and underline it on screen.

hooks.say: Three lighting setups for under twenty dollars. Number two is just a white sheet.
hooks.frame: The light shifting across your face as a sheet moves in.
hooks.next: Show setup one in under five seconds, including the price.

hooks.say: Six apps I deleted this year, and what replaced them.
hooks.frame: A phone home screen with icons disappearing one by one.
hooks.next: Name app one and its replacement in a single line.

hooks.say: Three notebook layouts that actually stuck. I tried eleven.
hooks.frame: A hand flipping through filled pages.
hooks.next: Open to layout one and point at the part that makes it work.

hooks.say: Four shots every product video needs. Most people skip the second one.
hooks.frame: Close on a product turning in your hand.
hooks.next: Show shot one, then make viewers wait a beat for shot two.

hooks.say: Two questions that tell you if a client is going to pay late.
hooks.frame: Your face, with the first question landing on screen.
hooks.next: Ask question one and tell the story of the client who failed it.

hooks.say: Five places in this city where locals actually eat. None of them have a sign.
hooks.frame: Walking past an unmarked door.
hooks.next: Stop at the first door and say what to order.

title: Test it on camera
why: An experiment gives the viewer a reason to wait for the result.
formula: I tried [thing] for [time]. [A hint at the surprise].
check: Does the video actually show the result, not just promise it?

hooks.say: Same clip, two edits. Watch where people swiped on the first one.
hooks.frame: Split screen with both edits playing in sync.
hooks.next: Pause both at the second where they differ.

hooks.say: I posted the same Reel at eight in the morning and eight at night. The difference wasn't what I expected.
hooks.frame: Two phones side by side playing the same video.
hooks.next: Show both view counts at the 24-hour mark.

hooks.say: I used only my phone for a week of client shoots. Here's where it broke.
hooks.frame: The phone on a small grip, recording.
hooks.next: Show the first shot where the phone struggled.

hooks.say: I made the same coffee with five different milks. One of them won't foam at all.
hooks.frame: Milk pouring into an espresso, close.
hooks.next: Pour milk one and score it on screen.

hooks.say: I let AI write my hooks for thirty days. My best and worst videos both came out of it.
hooks.frame: A phone with a chat window open, cursor blinking.
hooks.next: Show the worst hook first and the views it got.

hooks.say: I wrote by hand every day for a month. Day nineteen changed how I work.
hooks.frame: A pen moving across a notebook page.
hooks.next: Flip to the day-nineteen page and read one line.

hooks.say: I asked ten strangers which of these two photos was taken on a phone.
hooks.frame: Two photos side by side with no labels.
hooks.next: Give viewers two seconds to guess before the first stranger answers.

hooks.say: Can a ten-dollar sander finish this tabletop? Let's find out.
hooks.frame: The sander touching down on rough wood.
hooks.next: Show the surface after the first pass, up close.

hooks.say: I walked for thirty minutes after every meal for two weeks. This is what my energy looked like.
hooks.frame: Your energy log full screen, you in a corner circle.
hooks.next: Point at the day it changed and say what you noticed.

hooks.say: I tested three cheap microphones against my phone. You might not need one.
hooks.frame: Your face at a microphone, levels moving.
hooks.next: Play the same sentence on the phone first, then mic one.

title: Name the cost
why: Putting a price on a problem, in time or money, makes it feel urgent.
check: Is the number real, or clearly labeled as an estimate?

hooks.say: Re-recording your intro ten times is costing you more than the whole edit.
hooks.frame: Your face with a take counter ticking up.
hooks.next: Show how long you used to spend on the intro, then what you do now.

hooks.say: That subscription you forgot about costs you a good lunch every single month.
hooks.frame: A bank statement full screen with one small charge highlighted, you in a corner.
hooks.next: Show where to find every subscription in under a minute.

hooks.say: Exporting with the wrong settings is why your videos look worse after you upload them.
hooks.frame: The export window with the resolution highlighted.
hooks.next: Show the three settings you use, one at a time.

hooks.say: Cheap knives cost more than one good one. I did the maths on five years.
hooks.frame: A knife slicing cleanly through garlic.
hooks.next: Put the five-year total on screen, then the one knife.

hooks.say: Saying yes to small favors cost me about a day a week last year.
hooks.frame: A calendar filling up with small blocks.
hooks.next: Show the one line you now use to say no.

hooks.say: The hour you spend picking a font is an hour you didn't spend on your hook.
hooks.frame: A font menu scrolling endlessly.
hooks.next: Name the one font you use and move on.

hooks.say: Waiting for the perfect camera cost me two years of posting.
hooks.frame: Your face, with a camera box still sealed on the shelf.
hooks.next: Show your first phone video and what it led to.

hooks.say: One badly priced job can wipe out a month of good ones. This is the check I run first.
hooks.frame: A hand writing figures on a notepad.
hooks.next: Run the check on a real (anonymized) quote.

hooks.say: Bad file names cost you an hour every time a client asks for an old version.
hooks.frame: A folder full of files called final_final_v3.
hooks.next: Show your naming rule and rename one file live.

hooks.say: If you're paying an editor to cut pauses, you're paying for something a free tool does in a minute.
hooks.frame: A timeline with the gaps snapping shut.
hooks.next: Run the tool on a real take and show the before and after length.

title: Call out who it's for
why: Naming the exact viewer makes the right people feel the video was made for them.
formula: If you're a [specific person] who [specific situation], [what this gives you].
check: Would the person you named recognize themselves in the first five words?

hooks.say: If you run a small café and your Instagram is just photos of coffee, watch this before your next post.
hooks.frame: A latte being set down on the counter.
hooks.next: Show one post that isn't a coffee photo and why it works.

hooks.say: If you're a freelancer who hates sending invoices, this takes the awkward part out.
hooks.frame: Your face, then the invoice full screen with you in a corner.
hooks.next: Point at the line on the invoice that does the awkward part for you.

hooks.say: If you've filmed ten videos and posted none, this one's for you.
hooks.frame: A phone gallery full of unposted clips.
hooks.next: Pick one of your own unposted clips and post it on camera.

hooks.say: If you study for hours and forget it all by morning, try this tonight.
hooks.frame: A hand writing a question in the margin of some notes.
hooks.next: Show the three questions you write after every study session.

hooks.say: If you just bought a sewing machine and you're scared to touch it, start here.
hooks.frame: The needle moving slowly through fabric.
hooks.next: Sew one straight line on scrap fabric, slowly, on camera.

hooks.say: If your podcast clips get no views, it's probably the first line you picked.
hooks.frame: A host at the microphone, mid-laugh.
hooks.next: Re-cut the same clip from a stronger first line and play both.

hooks.say: If you work nine to five and want to start filming, this is my whole weekday setup.
hooks.frame: Walking out of the office building.
hooks.next: Show the gear in your bag in under five seconds.

hooks.say: If you sell handmade things online and your photos look flat, change the angle before you change the camera.
hooks.frame: A product turning slowly under window light.
hooks.next: Shoot the same product from three angles and pick one.

hooks.say: If you're a new manager and your one-on-ones feel awkward, steal these three questions.
hooks.frame: Your face with a short list appearing beside you.
hooks.next: Ask question one as if the viewer is your report.

hooks.say: If you edit on your phone and think you need a laptop to look professional, you don't.
hooks.frame: A thumb dragging clips on a phone timeline.
hooks.next: Show one move that looks like desktop editing, done on the phone.

title: Bust a myth
why: Correcting something people believe gives them new information in the first second.
check: Is your correction specific enough for someone to check?

hooks.say: You don't need a ring light. Half the time it's what's making your eyes look strange.
hooks.frame: A ring light switching off, your face lit by a window instead.
hooks.next: Zoom into your eyes with and without the ring light.

hooks.say: The algorithm isn't hiding your videos. People are swiping in the first second.
hooks.frame: A feed scrolling fast past a video.
hooks.next: Show your own retention graph and point at the first-second drop.

hooks.say: Hashtags won't save a video nobody finishes.
hooks.frame: A wall of hashtags falling off the screen.
hooks.next: Say what actually decides it, in one sentence.

hooks.say: Oat milk can foam just like regular milk. You're steaming it wrong.
hooks.frame: A steam wand in the jug, milk spinning.
hooks.next: Show where the wand tip should sit, up close.

hooks.say: There's no perfect time to post. There's a first second worth stopping for.
hooks.frame: Your face, with a spinning clock that stops dead.
hooks.next: Show two of your videos posted at the same time with very different results.

hooks.say: Long videos don't get punished. Boring ones do.
hooks.frame: Your face, with a progress bar stretching longer and longer.
hooks.next: Show a long video that held people and say why.

hooks.say: You don't need a quiet house to record clean audio. You need a wardrobe.
hooks.frame: You stepping into a wardrobe with a microphone.
hooks.next: Play the kitchen take, then the wardrobe take.

hooks.say: Expensive wood doesn't make a better table. Your sanding does.
hooks.frame: The sander gliding over pale wood.
hooks.next: Compare a cheap board sanded well with a pricey one sanded badly.

hooks.say: Writing things down doesn't make you remember them. Testing yourself does.
hooks.frame: A hand closing a notebook and covering the page.
hooks.next: Show the quiz-yourself method on one page of notes.

hooks.say: You don't have to show your face to grow. You do have to show something worth watching.
hooks.frame: Hands at work, no face in frame.
hooks.next: Show three faceless shots that hold attention and why.

title: Show it before you explain it
why: A strange or satisfying image does the hooking before you say a word.
check: Would the first frame make someone stop with the sound off?

hooks.say: This is a fifteen-dollar phone grip, and it's why my handheld shots stopped shaking.
hooks.frame: The phone held up close to the lens with the grip attached.
hooks.next: Show a shaky shot without it, then the same walk with it.

hooks.say: Watch the needle. That one setting is the difference between a puckered seam and a flat one.
hooks.frame: An extreme close-up of the needle and presser foot.
hooks.next: Show the dial and the number you set it to.

hooks.say: See how the milk folds over itself right there? That's when you start the pattern.
hooks.frame: Milk folding into the espresso, close.
hooks.next: Replay the moment at half speed with an arrow on it.

hooks.say: This page is my whole week. Every task goes through these three boxes.
hooks.frame: Top-down on a notebook spread.
hooks.next: Zoom into box one and explain it in a sentence.

hooks.say: This is the timeline for a sixty-second Reel. Count how many times something changes.
hooks.frame: A dense timeline filling the screen.
hooks.next: Give the number, then play the Reel.

hooks.say: Look at the light on the left side of my face. That's one sheet of paper.
hooks.frame: Your face half lit, with a sheet of paper entering frame.
hooks.next: Pull the paper away and back so viewers see the change twice.

hooks.say: This is the dial most people never touch, and it fixes muddy video.
hooks.frame: A thumb turning a camera dial, close.
hooks.next: Show a muddy clip, turn the dial, show it again.

hooks.say: Listen to this knife. That sound tells you it's actually sharp.
hooks.frame: A knife slicing garlic, close.
hooks.next: Play the sound of a dull knife on the same garlic.

hooks.say: This street has a café with no sign, and it's the best coffee in the city.
hooks.frame: Walking past a plain door.
hooks.next: Walk in, order, and show the cup before you say the name.

hooks.say: This is the wood before I touched it. Keep your eye on the grain.
hooks.text: Keep your eye on the grain
hooks.frame: A rough board with the sander about to touch down.
hooks.next: Cut through the passes until the grain shows, then hold.

title: React to a receipt
why: A real comment, post or screenshot gives you a conflict to resolve on camera.
formula: Someone [said or posted this]. [Your quick take, then let's check].
check: Is the receipt readable on a phone, with private details blurred?

hooks.say: Someone said my edits are 'way too fast to follow.' Let's look at the numbers.
hooks.frame: The comment full screen, your face in a corner circle.
hooks.next: Show retention for your fastest and slowest edit, side by side.
hooks.note: way too fast to follow tbh

hooks.say: This post says you need four hours a day to grow on YouTube. I spend about forty minutes.
hooks.frame: The post full screen, with the claim highlighted.
hooks.next: Show what your forty minutes looks like, step by step.

hooks.say: A client sent me this as a reference. This is why I said no to copying it.
hooks.frame: The message thread full screen, with the reference attached.
hooks.next: Show what you made instead and how the client reacted.
hooks.note: can we do it like this?

hooks.say: This chart is going around, and it's missing one thing that changes the whole story.
hooks.frame: The chart full screen, you in the corner.
hooks.next: Add the missing line to the chart on screen.

hooks.say: The meanest comment I got last month was right, and I changed my whole intro because of it.
hooks.frame: The comment card sliding in next to your face.
hooks.next: Play the old intro, then the new one.

hooks.say: This headline says nobody reads captions anymore. My analytics say otherwise.
hooks.frame: The article headline full screen.
hooks.next: Show two versions of a video, with and without captions.

hooks.say: My guest read this post out loud and we had to stop recording.
hooks.frame: The guest at the mic reading from a phone.
hooks.next: Play what the guest said right after, uncut.

hooks.say: A viewer sent me their first video and asked what's wrong. This is what I'd change in the first second.
hooks.frame: Their video playing on a phone screen.
hooks.next: Pause on frame one and name the single change.

hooks.say: This invoice is real, and it's why I now ask for half up front.
hooks.text: Why I ask for 50% up front
hooks.frame: The invoice full screen with the overdue date circled.
hooks.next: Show the line you added to your contract.

hooks.say: A shop wanted forty dollars for this. I made mine from leftover fabric.
hooks.frame: The shop version above, yours below.
hooks.next: Show the leftover fabric and how long it took.

title: Before and after in one cut
why: A hard cut between two states shows the value of an idea faster than explaining it.
formula: This was [before]. This is [after]. [The one change].
check: Are both shots framed the same, so the only thing that differs is the change?

hooks.say: This was my setup a year ago. This is it now. I spent less than you'd think.
hooks.frame: The old setup on top, the current one below.
hooks.next: Put the total cost on screen, then name the one buy that mattered.

hooks.say: Raw take. Now the same take with three edits. Watch your attention change.
hooks.frame: The unedited clip, then the edited version.
hooks.next: Name the three edits as they happen.

hooks.say: On top is how I used to pour. Underneath is after fixing my wrist.
hooks.frame: Two pours into the same cup, stacked.
hooks.next: Show the wrist movement on its own, slowed down.

hooks.say: This audio was recorded in my kitchen. Same mic, now in a wardrobe.
hooks.frame: Your face at the mic, then a door closing.
hooks.next: Play both clips again with the waveform on screen.

hooks.say: My desk on Monday and on Friday, with one rule in between.
hooks.frame: Top-down on a cluttered desk, hard cut to a clear one.
hooks.next: State the rule in one line on screen.

hooks.say: This thumbnail took me five minutes. This one got three times the clicks.
hooks.frame: Two thumbnails stacked.
hooks.next: Point at the one difference between them.

hooks.say: This board went from fence wood to a shelf in one afternoon.
hooks.frame: The weathered board, hard cut to the finished shelf.
hooks.next: Show the first pass of the sander on the old board.

hooks.say: This is my phone footage straight from the camera. This is after a two-minute grade.
hooks.frame: The ungraded street shot above, the graded one below.
hooks.next: Show the two sliders that did most of the work.

hooks.say: The first hem I ever sewed. Today's hem. Same machine.
hooks.frame: A wavy seam, hard cut to a straight one.
hooks.next: Show the one guide you added to the machine.

hooks.say: This is how I sounded on my first podcast. This is after one piece of advice.
hooks.frame: A host at the mic, then nodding along.
hooks.next: Say the advice on screen in one line.
